# Overview

**3 themes:** Computational photography · Light field · Coded aperture

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A[Monde réel] --> B[Optiques généralisées]
  B --> C[Représentation codée]
  C --> D[Computation généralisée]
  D --> E[Image finale]
```

::: {.callout-note title="Takeaways — Computational Paradigm"}
Optics + Computing are **co-designed**. The captured image does not need to be visually interpretable.
:::

---

# 1 · Computational Photography

## Plenoptic Function

$$L(x,\, y,\, z,\, \theta,\, \phi)$$

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $(x, y, z)$ | Spatial position (3D) |
| $\theta$ | Zenith angle |
| $\phi$ | Azimuth angle |

→ Space **5D** · One photo = a tiny sample of $L$

---

## Conv. vs Computational

| | Conventional | Computational |
|---|---|---|
| Optics | Standard | Generalized |
| Sensor | Final image | Coded representation |
| Calculation | Improvement | Decoding |
| Outputs | 1 image | $\geq 1$ image(s) |

---

## Pinhole Camera vs Lens

| | Pinhole | Lens |
|---|---|---|
| Sharpness | Everything in focus (∞ DoF) | 1 plane in focus |
| Light | Very ineffective | Effective |

**Conjugation equation:**

$$\frac{1}{D'} + \frac{1}{D} = \frac{1}{f} \qquad m = \frac{f}{D' - f}$$

---

## Focal Stack

**3-step pipeline:**

1. **Capture** — vary focus (focus ring or macro rail)
2. **Align** — correct magnification change $m$
3. **Merge** — weighted average by local sharpness

**Allocation of weights:**

- Apply **Laplacian** operator → local sharpness measurement
- Smooth the weights with a **Gaussian blur**

**Weighted merge:**

$$I_{\text{net}}(x,y) = \frac{\sum_k w_k(x,y)\cdot I_k(x,y)}{\sum_k w_k(x,y)}$$

::: {.callout-warning title="Trap — Zoom ≠ Focus"}
Zoom ring → changes $f$ (viewing angle). Focus ring → changes $D'$ (focal plane). **These are two separate operations.**
:::

---

## Depth inference techniques

| Technique | Input | Output | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Confocal stereo | Stack focus+aperture | Per pixel | Denser |
| Depth from Focus | Focal Stack | By patch | — |
| Focal Flow | Dense stack | Per patch | Effective, textured areas only |
| Depth from Defocus | 2 images | By patch | Minimal |

**Depth from Defocus:**

$$g_i = f * h_{\sigma_i} \quad \Rightarrow \quad \text{estimate } \sigma \Rightarrow \text{depth}$$

**Focal Flow:** biological inspiration → **jumping spiders**

---

# 2 · Light Field Photography

## Definition

The **light field** = geometric distribution of rays in space.

- Formalized as the plenoptic function on **5D** space
- In free space → reduced to **4D** via 2-plane parameterization

**Two-Plane Parameterization:**

| Plane | Role |
|---|---|
| Plane $st$ | Position on the main lens |
| Plane $uv$ | Position on sensor |

A ray = a couple $(s, t, u, v)$

::: {.callout-note title="To remember"}
The same set of rays can be captured by **plenoptic camera** OR by **pinhole camera moved** to multiple viewpoints.
:::

---

## 3 Capture Options

| Option | Method | Advantage | Disadvantage |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Camera network (Stanford Array) | Maximum quality | Expensive, bulky |
| 2 | 1 camera moved (LEGO motor) | Simple, economical | Static scenes only |
| 3 | Plenoptic camera | 1 single capture | Reduced resolution |

---

## Plenoptic camera architecture

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A[Subject] --> B[Main Lens]
  B --> C[Microlens Array]
  C --> D[CMOS Sensor]
```

- **Etymology:** *plenus* (Latin, “full”) + *optikos* (Greek, “vision”)
- **Inventor:** Gabriel Lippmann, 1908 — "integral photography"
- **Biological analogy:** compound eye of insects

**Resolution compromise:**

$$\text{Spatial resolution} \approx \frac{N}{k} \times \frac{N}{k}$$

→ $N$ = total pixels, $k$ = pixels per microlens

---

## Digital renderings

| Rendering | Microlens Operation |
|---|---|
| Aperture reduction (Stop down) | Sum only the **central portion** |
| Viewpoint shift | **Shift window** extraction |
| Refocusing | Sum windows from **multiple** microlenses |

::: {.callout-tip title="Intuition — Refocus"}
Refocus = shift the microlens windows before summing → areas on the new focal plane add constructively, others blur.
:::

---

| Component | Role |
|---|---|
| Lens Array | Microlenses |

| Light Field Engine | Dedicated processing |
| Marvell Avastar 88W8787 | WiFi + Bluetooth |

| Advantages | Disadvantages |

# 3 · Coded Aperture camera

## Objective

**1 single input image** → 2 outputs:

- **Depth Map** — by region
- **All-Focused Image**

---

## PSF and defocus

**PSF (Point Spread Function)**

- In-focus object → PSF = point
- Out-of-focus object → PSF = blur with **the shape of the aperture**
- Size of PSF ∝ distance to focal plane

**Local convolution model:**

$$y' = f_k \otimes x$$

- $y'$ = observed sub-window (blurred)
- $f_k$ = PSF calibrated at depth $k$
- $x$ = unknown sharp sub-window

---

## Challenges

| Challenge | Description |
|---|---|
| Smooth scene ambiguity/defocus | Homogeneous zone ≈ visually blurred zone |
| Ill-posed deconvolution | $f \otimes x = y$ has several solutions $x$ |
| Scale ambiguity | Wrong depth can also give plausible image |

---

## Idea 1: Prior on natural images

**Observation:** natural images have **sparse gradients**.

**Variational formulation:**

$$x = \arg\min_x \; \underbrace{\|f \otimes x - y\|^2}_{\text{fidélité}} + \lambda \underbrace{\sum_i \rho(\nabla x_i)}_{\text{prior}}$$

| Prior $\rho$ | Effect |
|---|---|
| $\|\nabla x\|^2$ (Gaussian) | Diffuse gradients → smooth |
| $\|\nabla x\|^{0.8}$ (scattered) | Locates gradients → sharp edges |

::: {.callout-tip title="Intuition"}
The sparse prior selects the solution that most closely resembles a real natural image among all those that are consistent with the observation.
:::

---

## Idea 2: Coded Aperture

**Principle:** binary mask in the aperture plane → pseudo-random PSF, distinct from natural images.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A[Ouverture conventionnelle\nPSF ≈ naturel] -->|difficile à discriminer| B[Ambiguïté d'échelle]
  C[Ouverture codée\nPSF pseudo-aléatoire] -->|clairement non-naturel| D[Discrimination fiable]
```

**Frequency domain:**

$$\text{Convolution spatiale} \Leftrightarrow \text{Multiplication fréquentielle}$$

$$\hat{X} = \frac{\hat{Y}}{\hat{F}} \quad \Rightarrow \quad \text{zéros de } \hat{F} \Rightarrow \text{division par zéro} \Rightarrow \text{ringing}$$

| Configuration | + | - |
|---|---|---|
| Without spectral zeros | Easily reversible | Low discrimination |
| With spectral zeros | Better discrimination | Difficult inversion (→ prior) |

**Filter Design:**

- Criterion: maximize **KL divergence** between different depths
- Constraints: physically feasible binary mask

::: {.callout-warning title="Critical point — Why “coded”?"}
Coded aperture reduces scale ambiguity. The correct depth is the **only** which gives a natural image after deconvolution. Bad ones produce clearly artificial artifacts.
:::

---

# 4 · Generalized optics camera

## Wavefront Coding

- **Replacement** of the lens with a **cubic phase plate** (cubic phase plate)
- PSF approximately **depth-invariant** (depth-invariant PSF) over a given range
- **1 single deconvolution** is enough for the entire scene

| | Standard lens | Wavefront Coding |
|---|---|---|
| PSF in focus | Point | Complex stain |
| PSF out of focus | Variable stain | Stable stain |
| Deconvolution | Local (by depth) | Overall (only 1) |

---

## Lattice Lens

- **Array of lenses** with variable focal lengths in front of the main lens
- PSF **non depth-invariant** → local deconvolution (like coded aperture)
- Captures a **useful subset** of the 4D light field

**Dimensionality Gap, Ng 2005:**

| Quantity | Dimensions |
|---|---|
| Full light field | 4D |
| Useful Image + Depth | 3D |
| Gap | 1D superfluous |

---

# General summary

| System | Entrance | Outings | Key principle |
|---|---|---|---|
| Focal Stack | $N$ images | All-clear image | Laplacian weight |
| Plenoptic camera | 1 catch | Refocus, multi-view | Microlens array |
| Coded opening | 1 picture | Depth + all-clear | Pseudo-random PSF |
| Wavefront coding | 1 picture | All-clear (wide DoF) | PSF depth-invariant |
| Network lens | 1 picture | Depth + all-clear | Varifocal lenses |

::: {.callout-note title="Common thread"}
All these systems share the same logic: **encode more information** in the captured image (at the cost of a degraded "raw" image), then **digitally decode** to recover what is of interest.
:::

---

# Key formulas

| Formula | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\frac{1}{D'} + \frac{1}{D} = \frac{1}{f}$ | Thin lens conjugation |
| $m = \frac{f}{D'-f}$ | Magnification |
| $I_{\text{net}} = \frac{\sum_k w_k I_k}{\sum_k w_k}$ | Focal stack fusion |
| $y' = f_k \otimes x$ | Defocus = convolution |
| $x = \arg\min \|f \otimes x - y\|^2 + \lambda \sum \rho(\nabla x_i)$ | Deconvolution with prior |
| $\hat{X} = \hat{Y}/\hat{F}$ | Frequency deconvolution |
